discovery: Dynamical mean-field theory of strongly correlated electron systems

nominees.name: Antoine Georges
nominees.affiliation: Collège de France, Paris, and Flatiron Institute, New York

motivation: Vollhardt (with Metzner) showed that the limit of infinite lattice dimensions gives a controlled, non-trivial description of interacting lattice electrons. Georges and Kotliar then mapped the lattice problem exactly onto a self-consistent quantum impurity model. The resulting dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) was the first unified, quantitative theory of the Mott metal-insulator transition. It captures both coherent quasiparticles and Hubbard bands, which static mean-field theories cannot. Combined with density-functional theory, DMFT became a predictive first-principles method for correlated materials: transition-metal oxides, actinides such as delta-plutonium, iron at Earth-core conditions, iron-based superconductors and Hund's metals. Its predictions, such as spectral-weight transfer and correlation-driven transitions, have been confirmed by photoemission, optical and high-pressure experiments. DMFT changed how physicists understand electron correlation. It is now a standard tool for designing quantum materials from fundamental principles.
